$comment: Cauldrons are both a capacity ladder and a parallel-brewing one. A better pot holds a heavier blend; a SECOND pot lets you brew two things at once. Buying one of each is therefore never the obvious move — a cheap second cauldron and an expensive first are different shops.
$capacityComment: Capacity has to clear 300 for the Sovereign band to be reachable at all: over-capacity caps a brew at grade D, so before these existed the top two potency tiers were a trap you could enter and never score in. cauldronFour is the first pot that can hold a Sovereign brew.
$stackComment: You may own several of the same tier. maxOwned is the total across all tiers, so a late shop chooses between many small pots and a few great ones.

tiers.$comment: The one you start with. A wooden bowl, and it shows.
Crystal-set, and the first pot that can hold a Sovereign brew.
Runed. Holds more than any blend the garden can currently supply, which is the point of an endgame pot.

$openingComment: The `opening` box on each tier is gone with the Phaser cauldron composition it positioned: brewing is drawn in the DOM now, so nothing needs to know where a painted pot mouth sits.
